name: Modal Cards

pad.note: the stage's own inset, and so the open card's margin

openMs.note: how long the card takes to grow into the stage. --motion-duration-base, measured off the reference at about 250ms.

closeMs.note: how long it takes to fall back into the row. --motion-duration-fast, and deliberately not the same as openMs: opening is the move that has to be read, closing is the one that has to get out of the way.

reach.note: the tour's walk to a button, and the beat it settles there. A loop length, so an option rather than a token.

hold.note: how long an opened card stays open before the cursor goes for the close button

rest.note: the beat after closing, before the next card's turn

cursor.note: mount the library's User Cursor on the stage. Off, the cards answer the real pointer only and the page keeps its own cursor - which is what you want anywhere the reader has one already.

accent.note: passed to the cursor. auto follows --navy: Tech Blue on a light ground, Innovation Blue on a dark one.

autoplay.note: run the tour when no pointer is on the stage

paused.note: stops the tour and the arrow together - pausing one without the other leaves a cursor pressing buttons whose cards never open

compact.note: the card-sized skin, for a stage under ~200px

methods.open(i): open card i, closing whichever is open
methods.close(): put the open card back in the row
methods.toggle(): pause or resume the tour, arrow included

reducedMotion: The card still opens and still closes - it is a control, not decoration - it just arrives instead of travelling: no FLIP, no transitions, and no self-driving tour. The cursor's click ring is skipped too, since there is no demo left for it to narrate.
notPorted: colour as a free value - the source takes any hex. Here accent is one of four palette names, or auto, and anything else throws.

a scale-based shared element. Measured off the recording the open card is 3.2x wider but only 1.9x taller than its slot, so a plain scale would turn the 15px radius into an ellipse and arrive with the body text stretched. The morph is a FLIP instead, and the title grows on font-size - a property, not a transform - so it stays crisp the whole way.

the card list as React children with per-card props. A card is any direct child element and the module reads it: first image is the media, first heading the title, first paragraph the body. The source stays a readable list of articles with the module removed.
brandNotes: Not a port. The source is React Bits Pro: the code is behind a subscription and its licence (§2.4) forbids putting the source in a repository or making it available to third parties - this repo is public and ships a reusable bundle in dist/, which is exactly the case that clause names. So the motion idea was rebuilt from the documented behaviour and a screen recording, on the Continia tokens. sourceUrl points at the page that describes the idea, for provenance, not at code that was copied. Timings were measured off the recording rather than guessed: the card grows into the stage in about 250ms and falls back in about 150ms, and the rest of the row fades out rather than staying put. The arrow is the library's own User Cursor, mounted rather than redrawn, per the pointer-demo rule in CLAUDE.md - an entry about clicking has to show the click, so user-cursor gained a press() that dips the arrow toward the surface for one duration-fast and pings a ring out from its tip. The reference cursor is the OS arrow and the reference palette is not Continia's; both follow --navy here.
blurb: A row of cards where one opens into the stage instead of a dialog opening over it. The card you click is the card that grows - it leaves the row, takes the whole stage and its body fades in underneath, while the rest dims away behind a scrim.
